content:
I wanted to run Trellis on a problem that would require autonomously building a lot of stuff missing from mathlib and also wanted to run it on one of the eval challenges that hadn't been solved yet, so I ran it on the unit distance upper bound challenge (which involved building a theory of plane drawings of graphs and proving things like Euler's formula, and then the crossing number lemma).

The public Trellis repo with every cycle edit is here: https://github.com/wpegden/crossing-consequences/

The mathlib version pinned to the challenge changed after I first downloaded it, so a single agent was dispatched outside this Trellis run to make the Tablet compatible with the version that was pinned at the time of submission. The challenge repo (just accepted by the submission site) has commits before and after this edit burst.

The same Trellis run formalized the other consequences of the crossing lemma szekely gives in his classic paper. They can all be browsed at the formalization viewer here:

https://www.math.cmu.edu/~wes/trellis/crossing-consequences-viewer/

This was 3 weeks on one ChatGPT pro account (no human input beyond providing an initial tex file, available in the repo, which was essentially Szekely but with a pedentic presentation of graph drawing background).
This topic was moved here from #Autoformalization > Trellis unit distance solution by Wes Pegden.
